Three methylphenidate prescriptions postdated September, October, and November even though all were actually issued August 14
One oxycodone prescription written with five refills to create the same 90-day result
Three methylphenidate prescriptions all dated August 14, totaling 90 days, with appropriate earliest-fill instructions on the later prescriptions
Three lisdexamfetamine prescriptions all issued on August 14, totaling 90 days, with later prescriptions carrying earliest-fill dates

stem: A practitioner sees a patient on August 14 and considers issuing separate future Schedule II prescriptions. Which sets are consistent with the federal multiple-prescription framework, assuming legitimate medical purpose and state law are satisfied? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Methadone remains Schedule II whether it is used for pain or for opioid-use-disorder treatment.
A pain prescription automatically becomes invalid if the patient also has a history of OUD
A valid methadone prescription for pain can be evaluated under ordinary Schedule II prescription rules, subject to applicable state law
An ordinary community-pharmacy prescription written solely for ongoing OUD maintenance cannot be treated as routine Schedule II pain prescribing outside the applicable narcotic-treatment pathway
A qualifying non-OTP emergency provision is a narrow dispense-only bridge while referral is arranged

stem: Each scenario involves methadone. Which statements correctly reflect how indication changes the federal pharmacy pathway? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Fill it as an ordinary Schedule II prescription because methadone prescriptions are identical regardless of indication.
Recognize that routine retail prescribing is not the ordinary federal methadone-OUD maintenance pathway and do not process it as a standard pain prescription.
Add five refills so treatment is not interrupted.
Reclassify methadone to Schedule III for this patient.
Sell an equivalent OTC methadone product instead.

stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacy receives an ordinary outpatient methadone prescription whose stated purpose is ongoing OUD maintenance. The prescriber is not operating through the applicable OTP pathway. What is the best response?

choices.text: The provision creates a three-day retail prescription that the pharmacy may dispense in a single fill.
No. The practitioner dispenses one day at a time for up to three days while arranging referral; no retail prescription is authorized.
The pharmacy may create a three-day methadone prescription after documenting the practitioner's telephone request.
The practitioner cannot use emergency dispensing outside an OTP even while arranging an immediate treatment referral.
The practitioner may issue a 30-day prescription and mark the first three days as emergency supply.

stem: A non-OTP practitioner uses the narrow federal emergency provision while arranging OUD treatment referral and asks a pharmacy whether the rule authorizes a routine three-day methadone prescription. Which answer is correct?

choices.text: Buprenorphine-naloxone remains Schedule III; the naloxone component does not make the product noncontrolled
Methadone for ongoing OUD maintenance is not handled as an ordinary community-pharmacy Schedule II pain prescription outside the applicable narcotic-treatment framework
Methadone and buprenorphine are legally interchangeable simply because both can treat OUD
Buprenorphine becomes Schedule VI in Massachusetts when used for OUD
A qualifying buprenorphine Schedule III prescription for OUD can use the ordinary prescription-dispensing framework when all current prescribing requirements are met

stem: Which statements correctly distinguish common federal OUD medication pathways? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Testosterone cypionate replacement therapy
Buprenorphine for opioid use disorder
Oxycodone for ordinary outpatient pain
Methylphenidate for a non-opioid indication
Lisdexamfetamine for ADHD

stem: Under current Massachusetts Policy 2024-05, which Schedule II/III prescriptions may qualify for up to a 90-day supply when otherwise lawful? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Gabapentin
Warfarin
Oxycodone
Alprazolam
Pregabalin

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing its next PMP Clearinghouse submission. Which dispensing transactions are generally included in the Schedule II-V/gabapentin reporting requirement? Select all that apply.

choices.text: It is collected for naloxone reporting purposes but does not appear on the patient's MassPAT profile.
Naloxone becomes federal Schedule II once it is submitted to the PMP.
The submission proves that all naloxone products require a prescription.
Naloxone must appear on the patient profile before the pharmacy may dispense another dose.
PMP submission is prohibited because opioid antagonists may never be reported.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy submits naloxone dispensing information with its daily PMP data. How should the pharmacist understand that submission?

choices.text: Warfarin
Insulin glargine
Gabapentin
Pregabalin
Methylphenidate

stem: A Massachusetts practitioner has a valid professional license and MCSR authorizing Schedule VI activity but does not yet have a DEA registration. Which prescriptions are within that Schedule VI-only credential situation, assuming no other scope problem? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The practitioner still needs the appropriate Massachusetts controlled-substance registration authority
A pharmacy dispensing gabapentin generally submits the dispensing data to the Massachusetts PMP
PMP reporting automatically converts gabapentin to federal Schedule V
The pharmacy must use the federal Schedule III/IV five-refills-in-six-months rule solely because gabapentin is reportable
The lack of a DEA registration does not by itself bar Schedule VI-only prescribing of gabapentin

stem: A Massachusetts practitioner with an appropriate MCSR but no DEA registration writes for gabapentin. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Stable buprenorphine Schedule III maintenance therapy when otherwise compliant
A three-day acute oxycodone course added only because it is Schedule II
An alprazolam dose placed in the package without checking any other packaging/dispensing requirements solely because it is Schedule IV
Daily methylphenidate used as a stable maintenance medication
Stable testosterone cypionate therapy treated as a maintenance medication

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing multi-drug single-dose compliance packages. Which scenarios can fit the current policy's Schedule II/III maintenance-medication allowance, assuming all other requirements are satisfied? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Yes, because every Schedule II medication is now automatically a compliance-packaging maintenance drug.
No; the relevant expansion concerns Schedule II/III maintenance medications, so the acute nature of this course must not be ignored.
Yes, because dental prescriptions are always treated as maintenance therapy.
No, because Schedule II drugs are still categorically prohibited from all compliance packaging.
Yes, but only if the pharmacy changes oxycodone to Schedule III on the label.

stem: A patient receives a short acute oxycodone Schedule II course after dental surgery. The pharmacy notes that Massachusetts now allows Schedule II and III maintenance medications in multi-drug single-dose compliance packages. Does that policy statement alone justify adding this acute oxycodone course to the maintenance package?

choices.text: Isotretinoin became an ordinary unrestricted Schedule VI prescription when the implementation date changed
The pharmacy must participate in the iPLEDGE REMS/certified pharmacy pathway to dispense isotretinoin
The patient must be enrolled and satisfy the applicable iPLEDGE requirements before dispensing
The pharmacy should follow the currently implemented REMS rules rather than assume the February 2026 modifications already took effect
The February 2026 modifications became fully effective on August 8, 2026 and must be treated as implemented today

stem: It is August 14, 2026. A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing to dispense isotretinoin. Which statements reflect the currently applicable FDA iPLEDGE situation on this date? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Isotretinoin through iPLEDGE
Mifepristone under the Mifepristone REMS Program
Sodium oxybate through its restricted REMS distribution system
Clozapine solely because the former Clozapine REMS still requires pharmacy enrollment
Warfarin through a certified-pharmacy restricted-distribution REMS

20 morphine, 20 oxycodone, and 20 hydromorphone units

26 lorazepam units

choices.text: 101 Schedule II-V analgesic units because one extra unit may be borrowed from the ancillary category
70 Schedule II-V sedative units because the hospice has fewer than 21 beds

60 units of approved lorazepam/other Schedule II-V sedative stock in the sedative category

stem: An inpatient Massachusetts hospice has 18 licensed beds. Under the acute-use ADD circular, its caps are 100 Schedule II-V analgesic units, 60 Schedule II-V sedative/anticonvulsant units, and 50 Schedule VI ancillary units. Which proposed category totals comply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Dispense untracked Schedule VI ancillary doses because they are outside federal Schedules II-V
Use an acute morphine dose for timely palliation while the pharmacy prepares and delivers the patient's full prescription
Reconcile a lorazepam dose removed from the ADD with the patient's prescription/order
Keep the ADD contents as pharmacy property until doses are dispensed for administration
Use the cabinet to avoid filling routine long-term prescriptions whenever delivery is inconvenient

stem: A Massachusetts inpatient hospice uses its acute-use ADD for morphine, lorazepam, and approved Schedule VI ancillary medications. Which actions fit the purpose and accountability of this program? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A PTT loads pharmacist-verified alprazolam with electronic validation under pharmacist direction/supervision
A PTT loads pharmacist-verified methylphenidate because the pharmacist is available by phone
A licensed non-PTT technician under pharmacist supervision loads pharmacist-verified methylphenidate with electronic validation
A nationally certified licensed technician, without prior pharmacist verification, transfers sealed non-patient-specific warfarin using electronic validation
A nationally certified licensed technician, without prior pharmacist verification, uses the same shortcut for gabapentin

stem: At an eligible Massachusetts hospital ADD, evaluate each stocking action independently. Which are permitted under the current technician stocking policy? Select all that apply.
